note: One file for the MSTX tab, the gap monitor and the TradingView indicator. Holdings and ADSO come live from api.strategy.com. btc_slope_per_2500 0.025 is Alex's sheet and matches the last three months' measured mNAV beta (0.81); it sets the projected price and therefore Cheap and Rich. lag_slope 0.0125 is DELIBERATELY different: the lag is a minute-scale deviation from its own trailing average, a different job from pricing a level, and it separates better at the lower slope. On 60 days of 5-minute bars at the bar low, distinct events 60+ minutes apart, 0.0125 at a -3.0% MSTX line gave 17 events (2.0/week), 65% positive at 60 minutes, median MSTX +0.49% and median MSTR-minus-BTC +0.28% -- the best hit rate of any slope and threshold pair tested. 0.025 at -3.0% was 13 events and 62% positive with a negative median on the market-neutral measure. Alex's call, 9/17. On 19 days of 1-minute bars the three slopes are statistically indistinguishable (10 to 15 events), so the 5-minute window is what this rests on. lag_threshold -0.015 = -3.0% MSTX, measured at MSTR's bar low (lag_at_low). lag_watch -0.01 = -2.0% MSTX, logged to the ledger without a push so the shallow zone keeps accumulating evidence. cheap_threshold -0.03 and rich_threshold 0.04 are MSTR terms; the Cheap and Rich tests run on the MSTX gap at twice these. regime_gate true governs LAG and CHEAP only, which is the rule Alex actually stated: use the buy signals when BTC is above its 50-day. rich_gate false since 9/17: Rich fires in either regime. The mirror-image rule that Rich should fire only below the 50-day was a symmetry assumption the system added, never Alex's, and it is the least supported rule in the file. Rich declined in BOTH states on the daily data at a +3% MSTR line: MSTR minus BTC over ten days -8.25% with BTC above its 50-day, -5.41% median below, five of six below-gate episodes down against BTC. The mechanism is why this is more than a six-episode backtest: Rich measures the premium to net asset value, which is the condition that mechanically triggers MSTR's at-the-market issuance, so a rich reading identifies new supply arriving rather than merely correlating with a decline. Caveat on all gate evidence: the STRC era is a downtrend end to end, so every above-the-50-day day in the sample is a bounce inside a decline and the gate has never been observed in a real uptrend. Correction 2026-09-19: Rich is weaker evidence than this note first claimed. Three of five Rich readings faded and the last two ran 25% and 52%; the two earlier runs above +5% MSTR lasted 46 and 41 trading days and widened first. Rich means ahead of the rule, not about to fall. The rule plus today's gap predicts the premium better than the rule alone out to about a month (see lookup_note). Review 2026-09-20 measured a -4.24% bare rule nowcast bias in chk_models_review.md, so gap_centre 0.04 centres Cheap and Rich on the rounded 4% MSTR premium and setting it to 0 reverts.
lookup_note: convex_fit is the HIGH end for the Bitcoin price lookup only: target = STRC base + b1*x + b2*x^2 with x = (BTC - 75,000) / 2,500, fitted in sample over the STRC era on 2026-09-19. Out of sample it lost to the straight rule (see mstr-mnav-model/2026-09-19-mnav-shape.md), so signals never use it. mstr_vol 0.75 is the annual MSTR vol used for MSTX's 2x decay over time: MSTX = MSTX now x (MSTR ratio)^2 x exp(-vol^2 x years). gap_half_life_days 28: the best estimate on the MSTX tab is the rule carrying today's gap, fading by half every 28 calendar days. Tested directly (mstr-mnav-model/mnav_gap_fade.py, walk-forward over the STRC era, 2026-09-19), mean abs error in premium points at 5, 10, 20 and 40 trading days: rule alone 0.083, 0.082, 0.083, 0.072; fading gap 0.039, 0.055, 0.066, 0.067. Half-lives from 28 to 56 days score within 0.003 of each other, so 28 is a choice, not a fit. About 26 to 33 test dates per horizon. Signals still use the rule alone.
